title: Chat & Messaging
summary: A chat system keeps millions of long-lived connections open and moves each message from sender to recipient in well under a second, in order, exactly once from the user's point of view. Messages are persisted before they are acknowledged, delivered over WebSockets to online devices, and via push notifications to offline ones.

walkthrough.title: Send
walkthrough.text: The sender's app writes a frame on its open WebSocket: { clientMsgId, convId, body }. The clientMsgId is a UUID generated on the device, used to deduplicate retries.

walkthrough.title: Route
walkthrough.text: The gateway already authenticated this connection during the handshake, so it forwards the frame to the message service with the sender's identity attached.

walkthrough.title: Persist, then acknowledge
walkthrough.text: The message service assigns the next sequence number in the conversation, writes it durably (idempotent on clientMsgId), and only then acks the sender. This is the single tick.

walkthrough.title: Find the recipient
walkthrough.text: The presence registry says which gateway server holds each of the recipient's device connections, or that they are offline.

walkthrough.title: Deliver
walkthrough.text: Online devices get the message pushed through their gateway's socket. Offline devices get an APNs or FCM push notification and fetch the message when the app opens.

walkthrough.title: Receipts and sync
walkthrough.text: The recipient's app acks delivered and read, which flows back to the sender (double tick). Reconnecting clients sync everything after their last seen sequence number.

data.label: Sender App

input.name: Ack
input.type: WS frame: { type: "ack", clientMsgId, seq, serverTs }

output.name: Message
output.type: WS frame: { type: "send", clientMsgId: uuid, convId, body, attachments[] }

responsibilities: Shows the message instantly (optimistic UI) and queues it in a local outbox until acked.
Retries unacked messages with the same clientMsgId after reconnecting.
Uploads attachments directly to object storage via a pre-signed URL, sending only the reference.

failureModes.scenario: Connection drops after sending, before the ack
failureModes.impact: The app doesn't know if the message was saved.
failureModes.mitigation: Resend with the same clientMsgId; the server dedupes and returns the original seq.

failureModes.impact: Constant reconnect storms drain the battery.
failureModes.mitigation: Exponential backoff with jitter; heartbeats tuned to carrier NAT timeouts.

data.label: Recipient App

input.name: Message
input.type: WS frame: { type: "message", convId, seq, senderId, body }

responsibilities: Inserts incoming messages by sequence number, so display order is the server's order, not arrival order.
Detects gaps in seq and fetches the missing range.
Sends delivered and read receipts in batches (e.g. 'read up to seq 812').

failureModes.mitigation: Upsert by (convId, seq); duplicates are ignored.

failureModes.impact: Thousands of messages to catch up on.
failureModes.mitigation: Paginated sync from lastSeq per conversation; recent conversations first.

data.label: WebSocket Gateway

input.name: Client frames
input.type: WSS: send | delivered | read | typing | ping

output.name: To devices
output.type: WSS frames pushed to connected sockets

responsibilities: Holds a very large number of idle connections per server (hundreds of thousands) and authenticates each at handshake.
Stays thin and stateless apart from its sockets; all business logic lives behind it.
Registers each connection in the presence registry and removes it on disconnect.

failureModes.scenario: Gateway server restarts during a deploy
failureModes.impact: All its clients reconnect at once (thundering herd).
failureModes.mitigation: Drain gradually (close sockets over minutes); clients reconnect with jittered backoff.

failureModes.scenario: Slow consumer (client on a bad network)
failureModes.impact: Outbound buffers grow until the server runs out of memory.
failureModes.mitigation: Per-connection buffer limits; drop the socket and let the client resync.

data.label: Message Service

output.name: Stored message
output.type: JSON: { convId, seq, messageId, senderId, body, ts }

output.name: Delivery
output.type: Publish to gateway:{id} channel | push job

responsibilities: Checks membership (can this user post here?) and assigns a monotonically increasing seq per conversation.
Persists before acking, so an acked message is never lost.
Fans out to each member's devices; large groups go through a queue instead of inline loops.

failureModes.scenario: Two servers assign seq for the same conversation
failureModes.mitigation: Route each conversation to one partition owner, or use a conditional write on (convId, seq).

failureModes.impact: Inline fan-out blocks the service for seconds.
failureModes.mitigation: Asynchronous fan-out via a queue; large channels switch to clients pulling.

data.label: Message Store

input.name: Append
input.type: INSERT (convId, seq, messageId, senderId, body, ts) IF NOT EXISTS

output.name: History
output.type: SELECT … WHERE convId = ? AND seq > ? LIMIT 100

responsibilities: Stores messages partitioned by conversation and clustered by seq, so history reads are one sequential scan.
Scales writes horizontally; chat is extremely write-heavy.
Applies retention and deletion (disappearing messages, account deletion).

failureModes.impact: Hot partition with slow reads and compaction pain.
failureModes.mitigation: Bucket the partition key by time (convId + month).

failureModes.impact: The sender's other device doesn't see the message it just sent.
failureModes.mitigation: Use QUORUM consistency for both writes and reads of recent history.

data.label: Presence & Session Registry

input.name: Lookup
input.type: GET sessions:{userId} → set of { deviceId, gatewayId }

responsibilities: Maps every online device to the gateway server holding its socket.
Expires entries via TTL when heartbeats stop, so crashed gateways don't leave ghosts.
Powers 'online' and 'last seen' indicators, with updates throttled to avoid fan-out storms.

failureModes.mitigation: Fall back to broadcasting to all gateways for small groups, plus push for everyone; messages are still stored.

failureModes.scenario: Stale entry points to a dead gateway
failureModes.impact: Messages are sent into the void.
failureModes.mitigation: Short TTLs, and recipients sync from lastSeq on reconnect, so nothing is lost permanently.

data.label: Push Notifications

input.name: Push job
input.type: JSON: { deviceTokens[], title, preview, convId, collapseKey }

output.name: OS notification
output.type: Platform push → device wakes and syncs

responsibilities: Wakes offline devices; the app then fetches the actual messages over its own connection.
Collapses multiple notifications per conversation and respects mute settings.
Removes invalid device tokens reported back by Apple and Google.

failureModes.scenario: Push delayed or dropped by the platform
failureModes.mitigation: Push is only a wake-up hint; correctness comes from sync on app open.
Send encrypted or contentless pushes; the app decrypts locally.
